title: ZTF 2018-2025 period changes of 1,706 Gaia DR3 Cepheids are mostly not evolutionary: Gaia 2014-2017 timing confirms about 40% of the curvature, and signs are balanced
abstract: We measured pulsation timing in each half observing season of ZTF DR24 (2018.2-2025.8) for Gaia DR3 Cepheids north of Dec -31 deg. 1,706 stars passed quality cuts (1,389 classical, 279 type II, 38 anomalous). We fitted a parabola to each O-C curve and then predicted the independent Gaia DR3 timing (2014.6-2017.4) from it. 13.3% of the stars have |z| > 3 for the curvature and 5.5% have |z| > 5, against 0.77% and 0.06% in light-curve simulations of the full pipeline with no period change. For periods of 1-8 d the significant rates are 0.3-20 s/yr, far above century-scale evolutionary rates. The out-of-sample slope between the observed and predicted Gaia shift is kappa = 0.35 (95% CI 0.28-0.42) for all stars and 0.47 (0.29-0.59) for |z| > 5 stars. The same pipeline gives -0.02 for simulated stars with no change and 0.91 for stars with an injected constant dP/dt. Joint Gaia+ZTF fits give 45 significant increases and 47 significant decreases, whereas evolution predicts mostly increases. At equal timing precision (P = 1-6 d), 10.7% of first-overtone classical Cepheids have |z| > 5, against 2.0% of fundamental-mode stars (p = 7e-7). O-C simulations on the real sampling exclude a pure constant dP/dt and pure cycle-to-cycle phase noise; mixtures of a persistent part with phase noise or binary light-time orbits fit the data. Gaia RUWE is only slightly higher for the changing stars. We list 29 stars whose ZTF curvature also predicts the Gaia epoch. Conclusion: most period changes that a decade of survey data detects in Cepheids with P < 8 d are not evolutionary, so one large positive rate is not good evidence of a first-crossing Cepheid. Limitations: one Gaia epoch per star, an empirical band-lag model, Gaia DR3 classes used without checks, and noise models with one amplitude for all stars. Raw Gaia and ZTF data are not bundled; scripts retrieve them.

Left: data (kappa 0.35). Middle: light-curve simulation of the full pipeline with no period change (kappa -0.02). Right: simulation with a constant dP/dt (kappa 0.91). Black points: binned medians.

Absolute period-change rates with |z_joint| > 5 (Gaia+ZTF, 2014-2025) by Gaia DR3 class; filled symbols are increases and open triangles decreases. Grey: century-long O-C rates of LMC (Rodriguez-Segovia et al. 2022) and Galactic (Csornyei et al. 2022) Cepheids. Dashed line: median 5-sigma limit of this work for classical Cepheids.

Six of the 29 persistent-change candidates. Points: ZTF half-season O-C relative to the ZTF linear ephemeris; curve: ZTF parabola; square: Gaia DR3 timing point (lag-corrected), which the fit did not use.
